name: Short Report
useWhen: Use this to report what happened, how a project is going, or what you found and recommend.

sections.label: Title
sections.what: A short title, plus the date and your name on the next lines.
sections.tip: Say what the report is about. Add the date and who wrote it.
sections.good:
Parking Lot Lighting Review
October 28, 2026
Prepared by Jordan Reyes

sections.label: Summary
sections.what: The whole report in 2 or 3 sentences, main point first.
sections.tip: Most readers stop here. Give the bottom line up front.
sections.good: Three of the eight parking lot lights are out. The lot is unsafe after 6 p.m. We recommend new long-life fixtures for all eight lights by Nov 20.
sections.bad: This report is about some lighting stuff.

sections.label: Background
sections.what: Why this report exists and what you looked at.
sections.tip: Two to four sentences. Who asked, what you checked, and when.
sections.good: After two staff members reported tripping on Oct 15, the manager asked for a lighting check. I checked the lot on Oct 20 and 21 after dark.
sections.bad: People complained so I looked into it.

sections.label: Findings
sections.what: What you found: facts, numbers, and dates.
sections.tip: One finding per paragraph. Use real numbers.
sections.good: Lights 2, 5, and 7 do not turn on. The other five are dim and use old bulbs that cost $60 each per year to run.
sections.bad: A lot of the lights are bad.

sections.label: Recommendation
sections.what: What you recommend doing next, and why.
sections.tip: Make your case with one reason and one example, then restate the next step.
sections.good: We recommend new long-life fixtures for all eight lights by Nov 20.

topics.name: General
topics.tone: Objective and organized. Facts first, opinions labeled.
dos: Put the main point in the Summary

topics.name: Incident Report
topics.tone: Factual and calm. What happened, in order, without blame.
dos: Give the exact date, time, and place
Describe what you saw or heard, and name who told you anything you didn't see
List who was involved and any injuries or damage

findings.label: What happened (STAR)
findings.what: Tell what happened in order, using Situation, Task, Action, Result.
findings.tip: Stick to facts. For Task, say what you were doing or responsible for at the time.

topics.name: Progress Report
topics.tone: Honest and forward-looking. Done, in progress, and blocked.
dos: Say what's done, what's next, and any problems
Compare to the plan or deadline

findings.label: Progress
findings.what: What's done, what's in progress, and anything blocking you.
findings.tip: Use three short paragraphs: Done. In progress. Problems.
findings.good: Done: we installed the new shelves in aisles 1–4. In progress: aisles 5–8, finishing Nov 6. Problem: two shelf brackets arrived broken; new ones ship Nov 2.
